chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Yusuf, from Zakariyya ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Al-Hakam, who said:

I heard a man asking Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and the man said: 'Someone says that he likes me, so how do I know that he likes me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Test your heart; if you like him, then he likes you.'
ai.seo_question: How can I know if someone truly likes me according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a spiritual principle of reciprocity, suggesting that sincere affection (*mawaddah*) in the heart serves as a mirror for mutual love. This reflects the Shia concept of *tawassul* and spiritual resonance, where inner sincerity often manifests in external relational harmony. The teaching encourages self-reflection (*muhasabah*) as a primary method for verifying the authenticity of social bonds.
